article_id: 154. Robitzsch (2022). On the Choice of the Item Response Model for Scaling PISA
target_variable: Country means and standard deviations under alternative IRT scaling models
performance_metrics: Model comparisons via AIC, BIC, and ∆GHP across 11 IRT models (1PL, 1PCL, 1PLL, 1PGL, 2PL, 3PL, 3PLQ, 3PLRH, 4PGL, 4PL, 4PLQ). Model uncertainty quantified using model error (ME), bias-corrected model error (MEbc), error ratio (ER=MEbc/SE), and total error (TE=√(SE^2+MEbc^2)). For mathematics, the error ratio for country means was on average 0.24 (max 0.66) and for country standard deviations on average 0.77 (max 1.58).

finding_id: 154. Robitzsch (2022). On the Choice of the Item Response Model for Scaling PISA#2
article_id: 154. Robitzsch (2022). On the Choice of the Item Response Model for Scaling PISA
target_variable: Country means, standard deviations, and percentiles under alternative IRT scaling models
performance_metrics: Information-criteria results: overall, 3PLQ or 3PLRH preferred over 2PL for model fit (AIC/∆GHP); BIC selected 3PLQ or 3PLRH across models. Model uncertainty: for reading, unadjusted model error averaged M=0.66 and bias-corrected MEbc averaged M=0.62 for country means; error ratio ER averaged 0.24 (sampling error dominates). For country standard deviations, MEbc averaged 0.96 and ER averaged 0.60 (model error more important); maximum ER=2.05 for Finland. For percentiles, ER averaged 0.60 for Q10 and 0.84 for Q90, indicating sensitivity of quantile comparisons to model choice.
